source.title: Canonical Face Embeddings
source.authors: David G. McNeely-White; Benjamin Sattelberg; Nathaniel Blanchard; R. Beveridge

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether face-embedding representations from independently trained models are interchangeable using linear and rotation mappings, evaluated with cross-model face verification.
record.gate_note: The paper reports pairwise cross-model verification results in several figures. It also gives aggregate mean TARs in the abstract and discusses specific compatibility differences in the text. Individual figure cells are not transcribed as numbers because they are figure-only.
record.test_reason: Fits linear and rotation maps between final-layer embeddings of 10 independently trained face-verification CNNs. These differ in architecture, training data and loss. The maps are evaluated by cross-model IJB-C verification against unmapped performance, which directly tests V4's claim of simple maps with little loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that face CNNs trained for the same task approximate a canonical embedding space, related by linear or rotation maps. They hold that the task is the primary, if not sole, driver. Design choices such as Partial FC label subsampling affect finer compatibility. They also note security implications for embeddings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses paired face embeddings, least-squares or orthogonal rotation mappings, and downstream IJB-C verification TAR; it does not test the original sources' methods or a scale sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Mapping constraint (linear versus rotation), model pair and relative performance, PartialFC label subsampling, and number of paired examples used to fit the mapping affect the reported outcome.
record.code_released: The paper says code to reproduce the findings will be released upon publication; no URL is stated.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Biometrics, Behavior, and Identity Science
record.problems: Only 10 models are studied, and the authors say preprocessing and implementation differences may affect mapping performance; systematic controls are left to future work. The evidence relies on downstream verification performance as a proxy for representational similarity. Many pairwise values are presented only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Individual pairwise results across 90 model pairs and multiple FARs are shown in Figures 2, 3, 7, and 8 but are not separately transcribed here; sensitivity values by pair and sample count are in Figures 4 and 9. Their narrative-level findings are represented in r3–r6. The paper also reports LFW pilot results in Figures 5–6; these are figure-only and were not separately extracted.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep. Only a qualitative remark that lower-performing or less complex models map less well to stronger ones.
Not tested: vision-only face models, no cross-modal data.
Not tested: no same-architecture seed comparisons.
Stitching, relative representations and mapping without paired data are not tested.
Not tested: no interpretable feature or circuit analysis.
Not tested: no alternative similarity metrics or out-of-distribution inputs. Results vary only by FAR operating point and fit-set size.
Plateau with scale is not tested. Causal attribution to the shared task is the authors' interpretation, not tested.

missing.what: FAR dependence: rotation maps are near single-model TAR at FAR 0.1, while at FAR 1e-3 lower-complexity networks represent complex ones less well. Failure cases appear at smaller FARs.
Asymmetry by model capability: the poorer model in a pair roughly upper-bounds cross-model TAR, and pairs farther apart in performance map worse. This is qualitative evidence related to capability.
LFW pilot: linear maps among four weaker models give accuracies of about 0.98-0.995, with sample-size sensitivity.
G R100 P1.0 versus P0.1: label subsampling barely changes single-model TAR but strongly reduces mapping compatibility.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Downstream verification TAR is used as a proxy for alignment. Per-pair values are figure-only. V7 is mixed: the aggregate is near complete, but specific pairs are incomplete. The authors attribute convergence to the task, which is consistent with V7's 'shared objective' explanation, but they argue this rather than test it.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep tests whether alignment rises with model size or capability.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
The study does not compare seeds of the same architecture to test shared features or subspaces.

Tests linear and rotation mappings between face-verification embeddings, assessed by IJB-C verification performance. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired examples.
Does not test recurrence of interpretable features or circuits.
Does not compare alternative representation-similarity metrics or out-of-distribution inputs. It varies mapping type and number of paired examples, not the similarity measure named by this version.

Reports incomplete and variable cross-model mapping performance. It does not isolate whether shared data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause the alignment, and does not test for a plateau over scale.

tranche.reason: Fits explicit linear and rotation maps and evaluates cross-model verification to test representational interchangeability through a different method and downstream measure.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate as an account of their interpretation; task primacy and subsampling explanations remain interpretations or hypotheses. Pair-specific mapping losses are qualitative in the prose; aggregate TAR preservation does not quantify geometric completeness.

statements.correction: IJB-C 1:1 verification; FAR 0.01; mean linear-mapped TAR 0.95; mean unmapped TAR 0.96; code release announced upon publication.
statements.problem: The IJB-C result and protocol are correct. The supplied text promises code release upon publication; it does not establish that code is available or independently confirm completed peer review.

statements.correction: Linear-mapped mean TAR 0.95; native mean TAR 0.96; downstream verification preserved with little penalty; some information does not transfer; no direct completeness or plateau measurement.
statements.problem: The near-native downstream verification result is correct, but its classification as challenging V7 equates task-performance preservation with representational completeness.
